units.text: Currently Robolectric will default to `LooperMode.Mode.PAUSED` behavior, but this can be overridden by applying a `@LooperMode(NewMode)` annotation to a test package, test class, or test method, or via the 'robolectric.looperMode' system property.

quotes.quote: Currently Robolectric will default to LooperMode.Mode.PAUSED behavior, but this can be overridden by applying a @LooperMode(NewMode) annotation to a test package, test class, or test method, or via the 'robolectric.looperMode' system property

units.text: | `PAUSED` | A mode that more accurately models real Android's Looper behavior. |

quotes.quote: A mode that more accurately models real Android's Looper behavior.

units.text: | `INSTRUMENTATION_TEST` | A mode that simulates an android instrumentation test threading model, which has a separate test thread distinct from the main looper thread. |

quotes.quote: A mode that simulates an android instrumentation test threading model, which has a separate test thread distinct from the main looper thread.

units.text: | `LEGACY` | Deprecated. use `LooperMode.PAUSED`. `LEGACY` mode is not supported on Android SDKs > Baklava. |

quotes.quote: Deprecated. use LooperMode.PAUSED
LEGACY mode is not supported on Android SDKs > Baklava

units.text: - Tests run on the main looper thread.

quotes.quote: Conceptually LooperMode.PAUSED is similar to the LEGACY Scheduler.IdleState.PAUSED in the following ways: Tests run on the main looper thread

units.text: - Tasks posted to the main Looper are not executed automatically, and must be explicitly executed via `ShadowLooper` APIs like `ShadowLooper.idle()`. This guarantees execution order correctness.

quotes.quote: Tasks posted to the main Looper are not executed automatically, and must be explicitly executed via ShadowLooper APIs like ShadowLooper.idle(). This guarantees execution order correctness

units.text: - `SystemClock` time is frozen, and can be manually advanced via Robolectric APIs.

quotes.quote: SystemClock time is frozen, and can be manually advanced via Robolectric APIs.

units.text: - Robolectric will warn users if a test fails with unexecuted tasks in the main Looper queue.

quotes.quote: Robolectric will warn users if a test fails with unexecuted tasks in the main Looper queue

units.text: - Robolectric test APIs, like `ActivityController.setup()`, will automatically idle the main Looper.

quotes.quote: Robolectric test APIs, like ActivityController.setup(), will automatically idle the main Looper

units.text: - Each Looper has its own thread. Tasks posted to background loopers are executed asynchronously in separate threads.

quotes.quote: Each Looper has its own thread. Tasks posted to background loopers are executed asynchronously in separate threads.

units.text: - Looper use the real `MessageQueue` to store their queue of pending tasks.

quotes.quote: Looper use the real MessageQueue to store their queue of pending tasks

units.text: - There is only a single clock value, managed via `ShadowSystemClock`. This can be explictly incremented via `ShadowSystemClock.advanceBy(Duration)`, or `ShadowLooper.idleFor(Duration)`.

quotes.quote: There is only a single clock value, managed via ShadowSystemClock
This can be explictly incremented via ShadowSystemClock.advanceBy(Duration), or ShadowLooper.idleFor(Duration)

units.text: A subset of the `Scheduler` APIs for the 'foreground' scheduler are currently supported in this mode as well, although it is recommended to switch to use `ShadowLooper` APIs directly.

quotes.quote: A subset of the Scheduler APIs for the 'foreground' scheduler are currently supported in this mode as well, although it is recommended to switch to use ShadowLooper APIs directly.

units.text: A mode that simulates an android instrumentation test threading model, which has a separate test thread distinct from the main looper thread. Otherwise it is quite similar to `PAUSED` mode. The clock time is still fixed, and you can use `shadowLooper` methods to pause, unpause, and wait for any looper to be idle.

quotes.quote: A mode that simulates an android instrumentation test threading model, which has a separate test thread distinct from the main looper thread
Otherwise it is quite similar to PAUSED mode
The clock time is still fixed, and you can use shadowLooper methods to pause, unpause, and wait for any looper to be idle

units.text: It is recommended to use this mode in tests that mostly use `androidx.test` APIs, which will support being called directly on the main thread or on the test thread. Most `org.robolectric` APIs that interact with the android UI (e.g. `ActivityController`) will raise an exception if called off the main thread.

quotes.quote: It is recommended to use this mode in tests that mostly use androidx.test APIs, which will support being called directly on the main thread or on the test thread. Most org.robolectric APIs that interact with the android UI (e.g. ActivityController) will raise an exception if called off the main thread.

units.text: 1. Apply the `LooperMode(PAUSED)` annotation to your test package/class/method (or remove a `LooperMode(LEGACY)` annotation).

quotes.quote: Apply the LooperMode(PAUSED) annotation to your test package/class/method (or remove a LooperMode(LEGACY) annotation)

units.text: 2. Convert any background `Scheduler` for controlling Loopers to `shadowOf(looper)`.

quotes.quote: Convert any background Scheduler for controlling Loopers to shadowOf(looper)

units.text: 3. Convert any `RoboExecutorService` usages to `PausedExecutorService` or `InlineExecutorService`.

quotes.quote: Convert any RoboExecutorService usages to PausedExecutorService or InlineExecutorService

units.text: 4. Run your tests. If you see an test failures like 'Main looper has queued unexecuted runnables.', you may need to insert `shadowOf(getMainLooper()).idle()` calls to your test to drain the main Looper.

quotes.quote: If you see an test failures like 'Main looper has queued unexecuted runnables.', you may need to insert shadowOf(getMainLooper()).idle() calls to your test to drain the main Looper

units.text: | `idle()` | Executes all posted tasks scheduled before or at the current time. |

quotes.quote: abstract void idle() Executes all posted tasks scheduled before or at the current time.

units.text: | `idleFor(long, TimeUnit)` | Advances the system clock by the given time, then executes all posted tasks scheduled before or at the given time. |

quotes.quote: Advances the system clock by the given time, then executes all posted tasks scheduled before or at the given time.

units.text: | `idleFor(Duration)` | A variant of `idleFor(long, TimeUnit)` that accepts a `Duration`. |

quotes.quote: A variant of idleFor(long, TimeUnit) that accepts a Duration.

units.text: | `isIdle()` | Returns true if there are no pending tasks scheduled to be executed before current time. |

quotes.quote: Returns true if there are no pending tasks scheduled to be executed before current time.

units.text: | `runOneTask()` | Causes only one of the next Runnables that have been scheduled to run while advancing the clock to its start time. |

quotes.quote: Causes only one of the next Runnables that have been scheduled to run while advancing the clock to its start time.

units.text: | `runToNextTask()` | Causes the next Runnable(s) that have been scheduled to run while advancing the clock to its start time. |

quotes.quote: Causes the next Runnable(s) that have been scheduled to run while advancing the clock to its start time.

units.text: | `runToEndOfTasks()` | Causes all of the Runnables that have been scheduled to run while advancing the clock to the start time of the last scheduled Runnable. |

quotes.quote: Causes all of the Runnables that have been scheduled to run while advancing the clock to the start time of the last scheduled Runnable.

units.text: | `runUntilEmpty()` | Continuously run all Messages on this Looper until its queue is empty. |

quotes.quote: Continuously run all Messages on this Looper until its queue is empty.

units.text: Robolectric's native runtime now includes Linux arm64 (aarch64) native libraries, so tests that use native SQLite (the default) and native graphics (`@GraphicsMode(NATIVE)`) can run on Linux arm64 environments, such as GitHub's ubuntu-24.04-arm runners, AWS Graviton machines, and arm64 Docker containers on Apple silicon. No configuration is needed.
